name: Customer-Segmentation-USA-EDA-
what_it_holds: EDA repo built on the Federal Reserve's Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF) microdata - household income, debt, and asset holdings by demographic group; the SCF itself is the Fed's public source, this repo is a worked example pointing to/using it.
why_useful: SCF is a genuine primary source for US household debt/asset composition by income tercile - useful as a slower-moving benchmark for consumer leverage capacity around travel spend, though this specific repo is a low-value student EDA wrapper rather than a data mirror.
themes: Consumer credit and BNPL: Klarna/Affirm public stats, Fed G.19, credit card delinquency, CFPB complaints dataset (Airbnb refund complaints), BBB complaint scrapers
why_all: SCF is a genuine primary source for US household debt/asset composition by income tercile - useful as a slower-moving benchmark for consumer leverage capacity around travel spend, though this specific repo is a low-value student EDA wrapper rather than a data mirror.

name: GET_INPC
what_it_holds: Python script pulling Brazil's INPC (consumer price index) series from the IBGE API and writing to a database. 0 stars, updated Jul 2026.
why_useful: Narrow but concrete: a working script for Brazilian CPI pull, useful for FX/consumer-strength regional split (gap #6/#7) if IBGE macro is wanted alongside BCB.
themes: Regional macro for LatAm and APAC: Mexico INEGI/Banxico, Brazil IBGE/BCB, Argentina INDEC, Colombia DANE, Chile, Japan e-Stat, Korea KOSIS, Australia ABS, India MOSPI clients
why_all: Narrow but concrete: a working script for Brazilian CPI pull, useful for FX/consumer-strength regional split (gap #6/#7) if IBGE macro is wanted alongside BCB.

name: pipeworx-io/mcp-estat-japan
what_it_holds: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server wrapping Japan's e-Stat government statistics API, described as 'e-Stat (Japan) MCP — government statistics'. e-Stat hosts Japan's CPI series including the accommodation/hotel-lodging component; this is a generic client, not a stored dataset, and appears extremely new (0 stars, created/updated 2026-09-13, one day before this scout ran).
why_useful: Could provide programmatic access to Japan CPI accommodation data, which we do not otherwise hold, if it in fact proxies the e-Stat CPI endpoints — but the repo is unvetted, brand-new, and generic (covers all e-Stat tables, not CPI-specific).
duplicate_of_holding: no — we hold no Japan CPI series
time_coverage: N/A (live API access, not stored data)
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: Could provide programmatic access to Japan CPI accommodation data, which we do not otherwise hold, if it in fact proxies the e-Stat CPI endpoints — but the repo is unvetted, brand-new, and generic (covers all e-Stat tables, not CPI-specific).

name: bls (Python BLS API client)
what_it_holds: Python client for the official BLS Public Data API (`get_series()`), takes one or more BLS series IDs and returns the pulled data; supports the free registered-key higher-quota tier. Generic — any CPI series ID (e.g. CUUR0000SEHB 'Lodging away from home', CUUR0000SEHC 'Owners' equivalent rent' or other CUxx series) is retrievable, not just a fixed headline number.
why_useful: A maintained, minimal client for pulling the exact BLS CPI lodging-away-from-home series (and any other detailed CPI/PPI item) with a specific vintage timestamp from the API response, supporting the point-in-time register rule; also usable for PPI Traveler Accommodation.
last_activity: described as under active/rapid development, no exact date in excerpt
time_coverage: whatever BLS series covers (CPI lodging since ~1997/1998 for the detailed item)
duplicate_of_holding: We already hold BLS CPI via FRED; this is just an alternate direct-API client, not new data
themes: Inflation and price indices for accommodation: BLS CPI lodging, Eurostat HICP accommodation, national CPI hotel components, Japan CPI, Australia CPI accommodation
why_all: A maintained, minimal client for pulling the exact BLS CPI lodging-away-from-home series (and any other detailed CPI/PPI item) with a specific vintage timestamp from the API response, supporting the point-in-time register rule; also usable for PPI Traveler Accommodation.
